title: Smoothness-Constrained 24L Chirp with Deterministic Warm-Start
scientific_hypothesis: Enforcing a maximum 7.0 nm absolute thickness difference between adjacent layers will produce a smoother refractive-index taper that reduces spectral oscillations in the 1530-1565 nm passband while maintaining high visible reflectance, and deterministic warm-start from round-1 best candidate with ±3% perturbation will prevent the score regression observed in round 2.
design_principle: Modified quarter-wave chirped stack with adjacent-layer smoothness constraint to suppress high-frequency thickness variations that cause passband ripple. Warm-start initialization preserves the successful round-1 topology while allowing local optimization.
proposed_topology: 24 finite layers: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2 on Fused Silica substrate, air incident
design_variables: adjacent-layer thickness difference constraint (max 7.0 nm absolute)
initialization: round-1 best candidate thicknesses with ±3% multiplicative perturbation
manufacturing_considerations: Adjacent-layer thickness difference capped at 7.0 nm for deposition uniformity
HfO2 and SiO2 are space-qualified materials
theory_basis: Quarter-wave dielectric stack principle for high-reflection bands
Gradient index smoothing reduces interface discontinuities
expected_advantages: Smoother spectral response in passband compared to unconstrained chirp
Preserves round-1 successful topology while enabling local refinement
known_risks: Smoothness constraint may limit optimizer's ability to find global optimum
±3% perturbation bounds may be too restrictive if round-1 candidate is far from local optimum
24 layers may still be insufficient for dual-band performance
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 multilayer stack on Fused Silica substrate with air incident medium. Layer sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2 (24 finite layers total). Initialize thicknesses from round-1 best candidate [52.925, 78.239, 46.246, 72.785, 56.794, 81.495, 56.456, 85.034, 46.691, 67.482, 55.395, 99.936, 80.226, 98.974, 64.858, 99.561, 79.560, 101.037, 65.886, 108.828, 81.886, 93.254, 72.435, 74.302] nm with ±3% multiplicative perturbation. Apply L-BFGS-B optimization with soft penalty on adjacent-layer thickness difference (max 7.0 nm absolute). Optimize for maximum transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and maximum reflectance in 400-700 nm band at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Run three optimization rounds with tightest_margin derivative penalty before unconstrained exploration. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers.
revision_reason: Round 2 showed score regression (0.9482 to 0.8317) due to reduced layer count (12L vs 24L) and quadratic envelope parameterization. This route implements exact feedback directive: smoothness constraint (7.0 nm adjacent-layer cap), deterministic warm-start from round-1 best candidate, ±3% perturbation bounds, and L-BFGS-B with margin derivative penalty.
